children.note: the children port exposes no parent session, so there is nothing to reconcile: this kernel has no parent (the host was never asked — `live:null` means NOT ASKED, which is a different fact from an empty list)

inflight.note: the durable in-flight ledger: `pending` is what the restart FOUND, `interrupted` is what it ended, `pendingNow` is what is still open

reassign.note: no re-dispatch policy was declared: the missing members are only NAMED (the assembly decides whether to rebuild them)

receipt.portsMeans: these are the SEAMS this assembly injected. A false here does not mean the fact is unavailable: the mailbox, for example, is self-persisting, so its count can come from its own durable key with no port at all (see `mailbox.source`). The `children`/`watchdogs` steps report `wired`/`attached`/`code` for their own reading.

restart.note: this process resumed an existing institute; the marker itself is durable under the "resume" key

receipt.checkpointing: not-implemented: resumeFrom is CARRIED (request → env → mirror → recovery re-issue) but never interpreted; segment/checkpoint semantics are the ENGINE's (cost/design in docs/15 §14.4)

carriedNotInterpreted: the token is part of the request fingerprint
resume.whatTheKernelDoesNotDo: it never reads, validates or advances the token: a changed token is a DIFFERENT request (fingerprint branch ③ ⇒ "interrupted, not auto-rerun"), never a silent continuation
resume.changeCondition: docs/15 §14.4: a real resumable engine exists AND a single job lasts >= the job budget. Only then is the upgrade "output protocol + in-run stream + a `checkpoint` field in the mirror + segmented re-issue + a per-engine `resume == one uninterrupted run` comparison" worth landing (~60-100 kernel lines + one demo per engine)

receipt.recoveryLease: enforced-by-exclusive-create (TTL = max(120000ms, job budget + 30s); stale leases are stolen)

procedure.title: 辩论会议 · 推荐流程骨架
procedure.subject: 辩论对象：命题卡 id（须含已写完的正式证明/证伪或已通过的 Lean 行）、一个文件引用（如 Members/<成员>/Propos/<id>.md 或 Lean 文件）。一句话命题不是对象。lean 已通过但概率仍非 1 的命题，辩论焦点是「代码中的命题与定义是否符合原意」。

steps.what: 各成员各自独立表态：给出该命题当前的布尔概率([0,1])、理由、以及证明/证伪进展。先不互相反驳、不互相引用（「独立」是**尽力而为的约定**，不是内核保证的隔离 —— 见 notes）。

展开辩论：轮流发言 / 举手后发言 / 主席邀请发言。★ 轮数由院士自行决定；本部署只给**动议次数**设了上限 `vmu.meetings.verdictMaxRounds`（默认 3，**任何 kind 的动议都计入**：topic/procedural/resolution 同占额度，程序动议会吃掉一轮辩论）——到限后新增动议会被具名拒 `VMU_RESOURCE_BUDGET`；额度只由这个设置决定——`extend` 延长的是发言、`extendlimit` 延长的是墙钟，两者都不增加动议额度，关会再开一场是另一场会议（额度从头算）。★ `extend`/`silent`/`end`/`hands` 是 primitive 原语，SERVICE 会议上具名拒 `VMU_REGISTRY_BOUNDARY`（primitive 注册表与 SERVICE 会面互不相通），发言界改读 `vibe_v5_say` 回执的 `speechBound`。

会议结束前，每位参加辩论的成员用 `vibe_v5_verdict` 交最终裁决：「布尔概率([0,1])，理由」——传 `meeting` + `proposition_id`（**不要传 `target`**：`target` 只认活票箱的 id，命题卡 id 会被具名拒）、`member` 填自己；主席可以用 `vibe_v5_verdict_ask` 通知还没交的人。★ 别把它和票箱混起来：`vibe_vmu_meeting { action: "ballot" }` 的票箱只对「待核验对象」开放——它的**决定性**票只认 1/0（(0,1) 的读数必须显式写 `estimate` 类型、且不进裁决均值）；票箱不是裁决通道，裁决汇总只读成员交上来的裁决卡（`vibe_v5_verdict_final` 的 `rulingSubmissions`）。
tools: vibe_v5_verdict { meeting: "<本会议>", proposition_id: "<命题卡 id>", verdict: <0..1>, member: "<你>" }
vibe_v5_verdict_ask { meeting: "<本会议>", proposition_id: "<命题卡 id>" }

steps.what: 框架裁定并通知：若全部一致为 1（或一致为 0）则最终概率取该值，否则取所有裁决的平均值；随后通知该命题卡的持有者把卡片概率改为该值。
tools: vibe_v5_verdict_final { meeting: "<本会议>", proposition_id: "<命题卡>", verdicts: [{ member, p, reason }], fidelity?: "conform" | "defect" }

notes: 本骨架是**推荐**：院士可以只做其中一步、改变顺序、或完全不用。框架不检查、不阻断、不记录偏离。

「单次发言版群聊」在本框架里就是「每人各说一次、互不打断」：会议内用 `vibe_vmu_meeting { action:"speak" }`（进会议记录），群聊形态用 `vibe_v5_say`。★ 但「独立」只是**尽力而为的约定**，两条事实要一起看：(a) 框架没有并发，轮次是**顺序**推进的（`kernel/turn` 的 drive 一个成员接一个成员跑），caller 交付模式下更是一格一回合（交回一份提示词、等一份回复，同一时刻只有一个待回回合），提示词装配也**不注入**别人的发言；(b) **即使顺序化、即使不注入前文，读房间仍然可能** —— `vibe_vmu_chat` 走 `chat.list`，内核的聊天读面**不按调用者过滤**，任何成员都能读到整个房间，包括同一轮里别人刚说的话。所以第 1 步的「独立」不是隔离保证：要隔离请用会议发言（进会议记录，工具面没有会议记录的读面）；靠群聊就只能靠这条约定。
发言楼层（谁先说话）是另一套机制：`vibe_vmu_meeting { action:"flow" }`（open/hands/round_robin/call_on）。骨架管议程，flow 管顺序，两者互不替代。
第 4 步不是自动的：`vibe_v5_verdict_final` 由**主席**显式调用（裁决必须有签名人），内核面 `vmu.meetingverdict` 只做算术与校验，通知走既有 mailbox 面 —— 本 pack **没有**在 `meetings.close` 上挂任何自动聚合钩子（"会议关了就把数算出来"会把一次显式裁定变成一次静默推断）。

receipt.agendaItemsSourceMeans: `agendaItems` are the lines THIS face joined into the stored materials (an array agenda keeps its items; a one-line agenda is split on the "; " separator the join itself uses). The kernel meeting object keeps its own agenda items (ids ag-1..., closable one at a time) and the kernel face reads them back — this field never claims to be that ledger.
receipt.formalAgendaItemsWhy: no per-item agenda was recorded: this meeting never declared a formal agenda, so there is no item list to read (the agenda, if one was given, is the `materials` line — read `agendaItems`)
receipt.formalAgendaItemsHint: to record a per-item formal agenda, convene the meeting AGAIN and pass an ARRAY of items through the pack door: vibe_v5_meeting { formal_agenda: ["<item>", { title: "<item>", kind: "review" }] } — that is the front door (its schema accepts a boolean OR an array), so the items are validated and stored by the pack; from the kernel face the same array is open({ formalAgenda: [...] }). A boolean (formal_agenda:true, or formalAgenda:true) only DECLARES the agenda formal and leaves the items as the materials line
receipt.formalAgendaItemsMeans: null: this meeting carries NO per-item formal agenda. The convene face stores the agenda as ONE text line in `materials` (an array is joined with "; ") and `formal_agenda` there is a BOOLEAN "the agenda came from a formal block" flag, not an item list — so null is the absence of an item list, NOT an empty agenda: read `agendaItems` for the items
receipt.nonAttendingMeans: these members are ON the roster but a deployment declaration (vmu.meetings.attendDeniedSeats: temp) forbids their seat to attend or vote: an attempt to attend is refused BY NAME, and the unanimity reading does not wait for them

invitation.means: the appointment notice is DURABLE MAIL (channel "mail", kind "meeting-appointment") written ONCE, by the kernel open(), never by this face: every member in `delivered` will see it at their next turn or through vibe_v5_inbox, and the notice line it renders carries the exact attend call. `woken` is always [] here — a wake is a live nudge and the durable row is the promise; whether this deployment injects a wake seam is a deployment fact, not a silence (RUN 198). `unreachable` lists the members whose row did NOT go out, with the kernel own reason; the convene still succeeded and the meeting is readable, so the repair is a message to that member — never a second convene, and a delivery failure must never roll back an academic act

receipt.noticesMeans: notified / notifyRows / notifyFailed are the kernel open() receipt fields, passed through unchanged (the kernel wrote the durable rows, so there is exactly ONE row per invited member and ONE notice line): `notified` names the members that really got a row, `notifyRows` names the mail ids, `notifyFailed` names every member that did not with the kernel reason. This face sends no invitation of its own — a second sender would be a second row
receipt.typeMeans: `type` decides the PROCEDURE (which skeleton this meeting follows) and is the word the institute uses; `kind` is the meeting BOARD label (sync/division/verify-request/solve-vote) and is what an archive files the row under. When no kind was passed the label is DERIVED from the type where the type names one (debate→verify-request, closure→solve-vote, division→division) and `kindSource:"derived-from-type"` says nobody chose it; a type with no natural label falls back to "sync" with `kindSource:"default"`. Either way it is a filled-in label, not a reading of what the meeting was
receipt.kindSourceMeans: no kind was passed, so the framework DERIVED "verify-request" from type "debate" — the label an archive reader would expect. No caller chose it: pass kind explicitly to override
receipt.rosterMeans: the roster is the INVITATION LIST of this meeting (who was convened), not the bench. rosterNarrowed:true means convene was given an explicit subset (`members`, or a non-empty `roster`) and the meeting read back exactly those members; benchSize is how many live members the deployment had when it was convened (0 = this deployment exposes no membership seam, so no narrowing can be shown). The CHAIR is seated by opening even when it is not on the list — that is why `present` can name a member outside `roster`; `attend()` later adds a member, and then the roster is the invitation PLUS the members who joined. `eligible` is who may vote: the declared voter seats (vmu.meetings.eligibleSeats) intersected with THIS meeting roster, or the whole roster when no seat rule is declared. A count cannot answer "who": these fields are the ids themselves.
receipt.atSourceMeans: no `at` was passed: the meeting opened at the kernel clock, not at a declared time
receipt.requiresChairProceedMeans: false: the meeting is already running — proceed() has nothing left to open; act in it (speak/vote/hand)
receipt.startReadsMeans: startsInMs is non-null ONLY while the meeting has not started (positive = the start time is still in the future, negative = it is overdue); elapsedSinceMs is non-null ONLY once it has started (>= 0, measured from the moment it ACTUALLY opened, i.e. activatedAt — not from scheduledFor); elapsedMs is an alias of elapsedSinceMs kept for old readers (null while not started, never negative). TWO instants are in play and they are NOT the same fact: `openedAt` is the ATTENDANCE BASELINE (the due time, i.e. scheduledFor, fixed when the meeting was scheduled) and `activatedAt` is when the meeting REALLY became runnable (the touch that completed the attendance rule, or the chair proceed). A scheduled meeting that had to wait therefore has openedAt earlier than activatedAt, and `startedLate` says so; `lateReads.openedAt` on an attend receipt is the baseline, and null while the meeting has not started
receipt.lateAdmissionMeans: lateAdmission is THIS meeting policy for a late arrival (a late arrival is decided by vmu.meetings.lateAfterMs against openedAt): "open" seats a late member and records late:true; "chair" holds the member at the door (pendingLate) until the chair calls admit(); "refuse" refuses the late arrival by name and names the two repairs (the chair admits, or the member joins the next meeting). THE DEFAULT IS "chair": a late arrival is institutionally a request to be seated, so the chair decides it, and the hold is readable as pendingLate instead of the member slipping in unseen. "open" is the permissive policy and "refuse" the closed one; a meeting row that was opened before this default carries its own recorded value and is not retroactively changed.
receipt.wallLimitNote: the meeting’s OWN upper bound, frozen at open: `wallLimitMs` is the value, `wallLimitMsSource` says who froze it (`convene` = the chair set it with durationMs, `vmu.meetings.hardLimitMs` = the deployment default), and `extendlimit` can raise it later: extensions ADD to the current bound, and a request that would pass `vmu.meetings.extendCeilingMs` (this deployment declares no value, so the runtime ceiling applies; the refusal itself prints the ceiling it used, as `after / ceiling`) is refused BY NAME (`VMU_RESOURCE_BUDGET`) — nothing is clamped to the boundary. `extendCeilingMs` is the ceiling in effect for THAT refusal.
receipt.sequenceMeans: the meetings after this one were declared IN THIS CALL: `index` is this meeting's position (0-based), `total` counts it, and `next` is the SEQUENCE ROW of the meeting that follows (`{type,kind,subject}` - the declaration, not an id: an id exists only once that meeting is actually convened, and the driver takes the row, convenes it, and reads the new id from the open receipt; null = last). Advancing is decided by the call that declared them, not by a settings key, so `enforced` names no policy for it.

receipt.note: the original could also PROPOSE a meeting from a non-chair seat and let the chair convene it; this face has no propose path (named gap: procedure/propose). ★★ THIS FACE ONLY CONVENES: for status/summary/snapshot/close/extend/extendlimit/proceed/lapse/ballot/speak/hand/hands/order/invite/invitedspeak/attend/flow/overrideorder use vibe_vmu_meeting { action, id } - the kernel face, which reaches the same meeting object. lateReads.arrivalMeans: TWO readings of the same room, printed by name: roster presence is "how many of the invited members are in the room", electorate presence is "how many of the members this meeting actually waits for are in the room" — the opening rule uses `opensOn` (electorate), and `missing` names the members still missing from THAT set
lateReads.requiresChairProceedMeans: false: the meeting is already running — proceed() has nothing left to open; act in it (speak/vote/hand)
lateReads.startReadsMeans: startsInMs is non-null ONLY while the meeting has not started (positive = the start time is still in the future, negative = it is overdue); elapsedSinceMs is non-null ONLY once it has started (>= 0, measured from the moment it ACTUALLY opened, i.e. activatedAt — not from scheduledFor); elapsedMs is an alias of elapsedSinceMs kept for old readers (null while not started, never negative). TWO instants are in play and they are NOT the same fact: `openedAt` is the ATTENDANCE BASELINE (the due time, i.e. scheduledFor, fixed when the meeting was scheduled) and `activatedAt` is when the meeting REALLY became runnable (the touch that completed the attendance rule, or the chair proceed). A scheduled meeting that had to wait therefore has openedAt earlier than activatedAt, and `startedLate` says so; `lateReads.openedAt` on an attend receipt is the baseline, and null while the meeting has not started

receipt.lateMeans: NOT JUDGED: vmu.meetings.lateAfterMs=0 here, so NOBODY is ever counted late on this deployment — late:false does not mean "on time", it means this meeting does not measure lateness
receipt.alreadyPresentMeans: this call is what put the member in the present set

quorum.capUniverseMeans: the denominator is this meeting's eligible members (3), because the ATTENDANCE floor can never exceed who was invited — the rule's vote floor is reported separately in voteFloor
quorum.capPolicy: min(quorumMin/quorumRatio need, vmu.meetings.quorumCap, eligible members of this roster) — the ATTENDANCE floor; the rule's 表决 floor is voteFloor.effective
quorum.presentNote: present = chair (seated by open(), so the house can transact at all) + members who attended or voted; presentBreakdown splits them, and `unanswered` names who has done neither
quorum.metIs: the FLOOR question only (present >= required) — it is NOT the institution rule; with required=0 it is true while nobody has attended. Read unanimity.met / the pack rule for the real threshold
quorum.metPolicy: met = (present >= required) — the FLOOR question (may this house transact at all); it deliberately does NOT fold in the institution's unanimity rule, because `met` gates vote() and requiring full attendance before the first vote would deadlock the house. The rule is `unanimity` below.

unanimity.deniedSeatsDeclaredMeans: the seats the deployment DECLARED as non-attending (vmu.meetings.attendDeniedSeats): a declaration, not a count — `nonAttending`/`nonAttendingSeats` name the members of THIS roster that the declaration actually removes
unanimity.nonAttendingMeans: no member of this roster sits in a seat that the attendance declarations forbid
unanimity.policy: the institution's rule is unanimity: the quorum counts as established only when EVERY roster member has attended or voted AND the floor is met (「未到齐则法定人数不成立」); the electorate is the roster minus the seats that vmu.meetings.attendDeniedSeats forbids to attend: such a seat cannot be barred from the meeting and waited for at the same time, so the ELECTORATE of that "every" excludes it — those members are NAMED in `nonAttending`, never silently dropped
unanimity.because: every roster member attended or voted and the floor is met

voteFloor.universeMeans: the vote floor's denominator is the INSTITUTE's voter seats (3), so inviting fewer people cannot lower the floor (this meeting invited 3 eligible member(s))
voteFloor.sourceMeans: the floor is the eligible universe (chair + residents, vmu.meetings.eligibleSeats); a positive quorumMin/quorumRatio only NARROWS it (min) — this is the rule min(用户设置数, 院士+常驻研究员数)
voteFloor.effectiveNote: the lower bound for a ruling is min(max(quorumMin, ceil(quorumRatio*roster)), quorumCap, eligible universe) — see formula; this is 表决人数 (rule L47), and it is NOT the attendance floor (`required`)

quorum.unansweredPolicy: members who have neither attended nor voted
quorum.note: unanswered members are named, never passed over silently (08 卷 D3/L4 口径); voting counts as participation

receipt.firedWaitersMeans: every waiter THIS call fired, with the delivery of its wake: `{ member, until, id, wake }`. Fired is a DELIVERY fact, not a promise that the member acted: vmu.meetings.wakeFailurePolicy decides what a failed wake means and the event is NEVER rolled back because a wake failed. The array is empty when no waiter was waiting for this event (the means line stays, so an empty array is not silent).

receipt.ranInOwnTurnMeans: true when this call ran from the seat own session, or when the kernel reported that a turn for this seat was actually DELIVERED and returned (out.turnDelivered) - the two facts that one key used to conflate
receipt.memberActedMeans: member "r-2" is the CALLER of this call, so the seat acted in its own turn: what this receipt records is that seat's own act

p1RulingReading.sourcesMeans: sources.submittedRulings counts the DURABLE ruling cards the members filed with vibe_v5_verdict — the same rows the tally reports as `submitted`. Chair-typed numbers are NOT cards: they are counted in `sources.typed` and attributed to the chair in `attribution[].source` (the count lives on the tally, the card count lives here, and neither is a substitute for the other). sources.motions counts procedure votes (motions/seconded/voted), which is a different record.
p1RulingReading.rulingCardsMeans: these are the durable ruling CARDS read for this (meeting, proposition) — what the tally calls `submitted`. An empty/null value here does NOT mean nobody ruled: a chair-typed tally has no cards at all, and the tally receipt already says so in `attribution`

p1RulingReading.meetingSettledMeans: this answers ONLY "is the MEETING closed": it is `read.state === "closed"`. It says nothing about whether a tally is decided (`tally.decided`), whether a proposition card is settled, or whether the ruling was filed.
p1RulingReading.settledDeprecated: the key name `settled` is kept as an alias of `meetingSettled` only for compatibility; three different questions were read off the word `settled` in run 58 (meeting closed / tally decided / card settled), so read `meetingSettled` here and the other two from their own faces
p1RulingReading.means: the meeting m3 was READ on this kernel: state open, 0 motion(s) (0 seconded, 0 carried), 0 vote(s) recorded; 0 motion(s) with a tally that is ALL FOR (no against vote, no abstention) and 0 of those already carried; it ALSO holds 2 SUBMITTED RULING CARD(S) filed for proposition rec-12 (all of them for it) — that is what the ruling name points at

receipt.p1RulingReadingMeans: this is the SAME reading the p=1 write will take when you copy `correction.call` back (its debate_ruling names this meeting): sources.motions + sources.submittedRulings (the durable ruling cards the members filed — a chair-typed number is NOT one of them) say what the gate will count, voted says whether it will find a counted decision, and means names it in words. It PREDICTS a read, it does not decide the card — so "my p=1 write will be refused for having no counted votes" is answerable here instead of by trying and being refused

floor.formula: min(quorumMin/quorumRatio need, vmu.meetings.quorumCap, eligible members of this roster) — the ATTENDANCE floor; the rule's 表决 floor is voteFloor.effective

gate.bitesWhen: it refuses exactly when the signers (the members whose number is in this tally plus the chair) are fewer than the floor kernel.meetings.quorum() reports — and because vmu.meetings.quorumFloorSource is "universe", that floor counts the INSTITUTE's voter seats, not this meeting's invitation list: convening a debate with fewer invitees does NOT lower it, so a narrower meeting reaches VMU_MEETING_QUORUM_LOST (measured: required 2 with 1 signature, and required 3 with 2 signatures)
gate.means: signed = the members whose number is in this tally PLUS the chair, who signs; the floor is kernel.meetings.quorum().voteFloor.effective (the rule 「min(用户设置数, 院士+常驻研究员数)」, whose denominator is the INSTITUTE's voter seats, not this meeting's invitation list) — it GATES this ruling: below it the call is refused by name, unless the chair deliberately rules on fewer seats and says why; the separate attendance floor (who must show up) is reported as attendanceFloor and never gates a ruling

floor.means: this is the VOTE floor of rule L47, read from kernel.meetings.quorum() (not re-derived); it counts the CHAIR because 「院士+常驻研究员」 is the denominator and the chair holds one of those seats. It GATES this ruling (see floor.gate): below it the call is refused by name with VMU_MEETING_QUORUM_LOST, unless the chair passes partial:true with why — then floor.gate.escapedBy:"partial" records the override instead of hiding it. `satisfiedBy` is signed >= required, where signed counts SIGNATURES (the members whose number is in this tally plus the chair) and NOT attendance: a ruling is not a ballot, and this floor is about who signed the number, not who sat in the room

receipt.floorMeans: this is the VOTE floor of rule L47, read from kernel.meetings.quorum() (not re-derived); it counts the CHAIR because 「院士+常驻研究员」 is the denominator and the chair holds one of those seats. It GATES this ruling (see floor.gate): below it the call is refused by name with VMU_MEETING_QUORUM_LOST, unless the chair passes partial:true with why — then floor.gate.escapedBy:"partial" records the override instead of hiding it. `satisfiedBy` is signed >= required, where signed counts SIGNATURES (the members whose number is in this tally plus the chair) and NOT attendance: a ruling is not a ballot, and this floor is about who signed the number, not who sat in the room

correction.pathMeans: proposition "rec-12" is a records row, not a library card: there is no file to edit, so the correction is the call above (the records face owns that row)
correction.call: vibe_v5_record_proposition { id: "rec-12", statement: "前 n 个奇数之和 = n^2（仿真占位，不声称已证明）", value: "对任意正整数 n", motive: "仿真：给裁决链一张可被裁决的卡（不是数学主张）", p: 1, debate_ruling: { subject: "rec-12", value: 1, mode: "unanimous", n: 2, decided: true, at: "2027-01-15T08:00:00.000Z", ballotId: "tally-m3-rec-12", meeting: "m3", by: "r-acad" } }
correction.ballotIdMeans: the `ballotId` above is the RULING AGGREGATE NAME (`tally-<meeting>-<card>`), never a ballot BOX id: a meeting box id (`b-…` from the meeting face) is refused in that slot by name — name the MEETING instead, which this same call also carries
correction.shapeMeans: one ruling carries ONE reference; this framework accepts it under two names — `ballotId` (a ballot/tally id) and `meeting` (the convened meeting), and the write receipt reads back whichever was given as `p1RulingRef`. The call above is accepted AS PRINTED: both keys are present, and they name the same decision.
correction.callMeans: every field in `call` is carried from the CARD, not re-derived: a numeric value prints as a number, a text value prints as a quoted JSON string (so it parses back to the same text), and a field the card does not hold is left at the documented default. If your card's `value` is prose, the printed call keeps that prose — it never becomes a non-number and it never silently becomes 1. `at` is THIS receipt's own timestamp (the moment the ruling was read) and is optional: omit it and the write uses the current time — the call stays valid as printed, and the string is a real ISO time, not a placeholder

warrantFor.useAs: the `warrant` argument of `vibe_v5_verified_promote` (the aggregate tally of this ruling, not one member's card)
warrantFor.durable: this id is a NAME for the aggregate, not a records row — nothing is stored under it. # v5r-report-duty
【汇报纪律：本所「动作覆盖仿真所」】
· **主动汇报是成员义务**：进展、发现与卡点写进自己的 Progress/，关键结论在群聊里说出来——所办据此派回合、领头人据此决策（统筹是安排谁做，不是替谁做）——**自动汇报是被声明的**（`vmu.report.enabled` 与触发条件写在部署配置里，不靠自觉）。
· **对外出口只有所办**：人类只与所办对话；要对外说什么先说给所内，由所办原样转达。
· **参数面属于所办**：`vibe_vmu_report` 只改 `vmu.report.params` 声明的域，且只有 `vmu.report.whoMayChange` 声明的人能改；成员可查看（action=status/declarations/trace），改不动。
· **特权经请示（由所办向用户请示）**：扩编、删档、跨库改动、对外承诺等闸门不要绕过；`vibe_vmu_human` 查是否在等批（`approvalState`／`queue`），`vmu.human.gatedActions` 声明的动作获批前**不执行**（`VMU_HUMAN_APPROVAL_PENDING`，超时 hold）。
· **「有进展就唤起所办」不会自己发生**：`vmu.report.enabled` 默认 false、`vmu.report.reports` 默认空；触发只有 `event`／`period`／`threshold`，报告只提示不做决定（`drives:false`）。
· **改参数是所办的事**：入口是 `vibe_v5_set`（一次一个**已声明**的键）与 `vibe_vmu_report` 的参数面——**改参数、控研究所是所办的事**，不是席位的事。
· **汇报不等于结论**：汇报不改变任何对象的真值；进 Verified/ 仍须满足既定票数规则。

# v5r-charter-roster-snapshot
  你入职时的在册编制（这是一份**快照**，此后可能变化）：
- r-acad · chair
- r-1 · member
- r-2 · member
receipt.callerIsSeatMeans: this key answers ONE question: did this call run from the named seat and its own session? It does not say whether the seat carried the act out - that is what a delivered turn (turnReceipts, deliveryPath) answers
receipt.ranInOwnTurnMeans: true when this call ran from the seat own session, or when the kernel reported that a turn for this seat was actually DELIVERED and returned (out.turnDelivered) - the two facts that one key used to conflate
receipt.memberActedMeans: this call ran from the OFFICE (a root session, which is not a seat) and named member "r-1": the record was written IN THAT SEAT'S NAME, but the seat did not act in its own turn. `memberActed:false` states that difference - orchestrating on a seat's behalf is not the same act as carrying it out, and a reader who needs the seat's own judgement should ask for it in a turn of that seat

unavailable.why: no refusal code was recorded for this turn (an empty `codes` list means "nothing was refused here", not "every field applied")

turnReceipts.deliveryUnavailableMeans: 投递不可用（why:not-configured）：本轮成员未运行，任何写入都不是成员在自己的会话里完成的（所办代转或不可证），所以 workShareOf 把这一行的 write 计入 unknownActs，不算成员发言。

noReplyShape.message: a reply verdict has NO usable shape: a ballot box needs the box id and the name of the voter (ballotbox.cast reads boxId and by), and this field carries neither, so the kernel is asked to skip it by name BEFORE any face is touched — no vote is cast and the turn completes; the seat rule (a temporary worker has no vote, rule L3) lives on the tool face, where a non-voter is refused with VMU_NOT_PERMITTED
noReplyShape.hint: cast through the tool face, which is where the seat rule is enforced: vibe_v5_verdict { target: "<live ballot id>", verdict: 1|0, reason, member } for a ballot, or vibe_v5_poll_vote { ballot_id, choice, member } for a poll box (a seat without a vote is refused BY NAME there)

noReplyShape.message: vmu.tasks.transition(id, to) takes POSITIONAL arguments, and a reply field carries ONE value: the dispatch would hand the whole payload to the first positional slot
noReplyShape.hint: use the tool face vibe_v5_task_update { task_id, expected_revision, action } — it maps claim/reassign/assign/transition/complete/reopen/set_dependencies onto the real transition and requires the revision token

noReplyShape.message: this reply field carries no meeting reference, so the framework cannot dispatch it without inventing one
noReplyShape.hint: use the meeting tool face: vibe_vmu_meeting { action: "hand" | "hands" | "invite", id: "<meeting id>", ... } — the actor and the meeting are explicit there, and the chair rail applies to an invitation

noReplyShape.message: this reply field carries no meeting reference, so the framework cannot dispatch it without inventing one
noReplyShape.hint: use the meeting tool face: vibe_vmu_meeting { action: "hand" | "hands" | "invite", id: "<meeting id>", ... } — the actor and the meeting are explicit there, and the chair rail applies to an invitation

noReplyShape.message: a reply carries no actor and no chair, and this field has NO usable shape: the kernel is asked to skip it by name BEFORE any face is touched, so no meeting is created and the turn completes (the CHAIRLESS convene path it used to reach is the one path that deliberately does not police seats, which is why it is not reached any more); the seat policy lives on the tool face, where a non-chair seat is refused with VMU_NOT_PERMITTED
noReplyShape.hint: convene through the tool face, which is where the seat policy is enforced: vibe_v5_meeting { action: "convene", member: "<your id>", … } (a non-chair seat is refused BY NAME there, VMU_NOT_PERMITTED)

noReplyShape.message: vmu.tasks.transition(id, to) takes POSITIONAL arguments, and a reply field carries ONE value: the dispatch would hand the whole payload to the first positional slot
noReplyShape.hint: use the tool face vibe_v5_task_update { task_id, expected_revision, action: "claim" } — blocked_by dependencies are refused there by name

noReplyShape.message: vmu.tasks.transition(id, to) takes POSITIONAL arguments, and a reply field carries ONE value: the dispatch would hand the whole payload to the first positional slot
noReplyShape.hint: use the tool face vibe_v5_task_update { task_id, expected_revision, action: "complete" } — from `assigned` you must go through `doing` first (the legal table is open→assigned|doing, assigned→doing|open, doing→done|assigned)

noReplyShape.message: vmu.tasks.assign(id, who) takes POSITIONAL arguments, and a reply field carries ONE value: the dispatch would hand the whole payload to the first positional slot
noReplyShape.hint: use the tool face vibe_v5_assign { to, subject|task_id, why, acceptance } — why and acceptance are REQUIRED and are mailed to the assignee

noReplyShape.message: vmu.meetings.warn(meeting, …) takes POSITIONAL arguments, and a reply field carries ONE value: the dispatch would hand the whole payload to the first positional slot
noReplyShape.hint: use the tool face vibe_v5_nudge { to, why, next_step } — it wakes one member with a stated reason and a concrete next step

noReplyShape.message: an objection in a reply would be dispatched as MEETING SPEECH (vmu.meetings.speak), and a reply carries no meeting: on an ordinary round it is skipped as no-meeting-bound, so it can never reach the voters it promises to broadcast to
noReplyShape.hint: file the reason where the ledger keeps it: the tool face vibe_v5_record_progress (track "obstacles", with member) records why the assignment is contested, and raise it in a meeting round through vibe_v5_say — the task is executed regardless, that is the semantics of an objection

counts.deliveredMeans: settled deliveries: the seam returned an answer or an awaiting envelope. A THROW is counted in deliveryFailed, never here

deliveryLastFail.message: the host exposes no subagents service at all (ctx.get('subagents') returned nothing), so no member turn can be delivered

writesWindow.readWith: vibe_vmu_records { action:"list", by:"<the by above>", since:"<the from above>", until:"<the to above>", limit:0 }
writesWindow.readWithMeans: this call is the one that answers this window: it filters by WRITER and by LAST-WRITE TIME, and the head list folds the shared durable store on every read, so a write that reached the store appears here. An EMPTY answer therefore proves one of two things and this receipt cannot tell you which: the member wrote nothing in that window, or this deployment does not share its records store with the member kernel — copy the answer and say which one you can prove. Before RUN 243 this sentence named no makeable query: the list had no writer or time filter at all
writesWindow.means: a member turn runs in the member's OWN kernel, so anything it wrote is in the records fold under that member id; this receipt cannot list it. Follow `readWith` before concluding the turn produced nothing - run 65 had a timed-out turn that had already written a draft and a progress row

deliveryLastFail.means: the delivery seam threw, so this turn is neither delivered nor answered: it is NOT counted in delivered, parsed or notExecuted. Counts alone will not show it again — read deliveryLastFail, and read `writesWindow` before judging that the member did nothing

counts.failedMeans: replies that ARRIVED but whose write-back threw (a malformed reply field is the usual cause). It is NOT deliveryFailed: the member did answer. Read failedLast for the reason and the text the member actually wrote
counts.replyParseFailedMeans: the reply ARRIVED but could not be parsed into the declared reply shape (no fence, or a brace span that is not json). The member's own text is in replyExcerpt (bounded to the same size as failedLast.replyText); `fields`/`executed` do not exist for such a round because nothing was applied

lastAttribution.attribution: no turn has been delivered yet
lastAttribution.attemptedMemberMeans: a delivery was ATTEMPTED for this member and has not returned, so it is not a claim about the last delivery: `member`/`turn` stay null until one does
lastAttribution.slotMeans: lastAttribution describes the LAST DELIVERY THAT RETURNED, and its member/turn/childId are stamped together when that delivery returns - so a turn whose seam is still in flight is NOT described here (read op:"status" turnLoop for the turn that is holding the lock, and turnReceipts for every turn this kernel opened)

status.attributionMeans: the turn engine keeps ONE attribution slot: lastAttribution describes the MOST RECENT delivery only, not every member's last turn. Per-member history is not retained here - `woken` and `counts` are tallies, and `memberSessions` maps a member to the child session that played its last turn

classifiedBy.member: row.deliveryPath is a non-empty string other than "caller": the seat own session (or a host subagent running as that seat) delivered the turn. This is a row-level reading of the same field the delivery seam reports.
classifiedBy.office-relayed: row.deliveryPath === "caller": the CALLING session played this member turn (deliverByReturning parks the prompt and returns deliveryPath "caller"; attribution says supplied-by-caller). This is the relay case.
classifiedBy.unknown: row.deliveryPath is absent or empty: the ledger does not say who ran the turn, so the writes are counted as unknown and NEVER folded into member. The per-call facts (callerIsSeat / ranInOwnTurn / memberActed / actedForMember) live on TOOL receipts, not on a turn row, and this aggregate does not pretend to read them.
classifiedBy.delivery-unavailable: row.deliveryUnavailable === true: the delivery seam never handed this turn to the member (timeout / error / not-configured / engine-lost-reply), so the member did not run and any write on this row has PROVENANCE UNKNOWN. This class is read BEFORE deliveryPath on purpose: a broken delivery is not a route, and such a row must never be laundered into "caller" (which means the office CHOSE to play the turn).

memberWorkShare.means: memberShare = memberActs / (memberActs + officeRelayedActs); unknownActs is NOT in that denominator, so an unproven write can neither inflate nor dilute the ratio - it is reported beside it. memberActs are the record writes in settled turns whose row-level deliveryPath says the SEAT OWN SESSION ran them (activation / continuation / one-shot / any host seam name other than caller). officeRelayedActs are the writes in turns whose deliveryPath is "caller": the calling session played this member turn (deliverByReturning, supplied-by-caller), so the office wrote on the member behalf. unknownActs are the writes in turns whose row carries no deliveryPath (legacy row, or a seam that did not say): who ran them is not provable here, so they are NOT counted as member. acts is the sum of the three; memberTurns / officeRelayedTurns / unknownTurns count the rows. A null memberShare means both proven sides are zero (nothing to divide) - not a perfect score and not a zero score.

turnLoop.parkedMeans: a caller-played prompt is PARKED on this session and is waiting to be answered: inFlight can be false at the same time (the lock is released when the prompt goes back to the caller). Answer it with op:"step" carrying the reply (that CONTINUES the parked turn - same turnId/member/promptId) or close it with op:"abandon"; a second op:"drive"/op:"step" without an answer is refused VMU_TURN_ALREADY_PARKED rather than overwriting it
turnLoop.openTurnsMeans: rows in turnReceipts whose status is still "open": a turn that was opened and never settled. A parked turn is expected to hold ONE such row until it is answered, released or timed out; a row that stays open while nothing is parked and nothing is in flight is an ORPHAN (its delivery returned without settling it - e.g. a resumed reply the channel could not parse) and this loop can leave that state by naming it: op:"abandon" with { turn: "<id>" } settles exactly that row (RUN 257), reading turnReceipts for the ids and their openedBy
turnLoop.deliveryBudgetSource: vmu.turn.deliveryTimeoutMs default (1800000 ms, declared in settings/schema.js - the same declaration the kernel loop, the v3 planner and the one-shot delivery seam all read)
turnLoop.timeoutOrderMeans: the delivery seam gives up at deliverySeamBudgetMs (2250000 ms = deliveryTimeoutMs + 25%) and THROWS, which releases the lock on its own; abandonAfterMs (2400000 ms) is deliberately LARGER, so it only fires for a seam that neither returns nor throws. In a deployment where the seam times out normally, this backstop is never reached and the delivery timeout is what releases the loop - do not read abandonAfterMs as "how long a caller must wait"
turnLoop.wakeQueueMeans: a wake that fired while the loop was busy waits here (it is never driven from inside another turn): it runs the moment the in-flight turn settles
turnLoop.lateAnswersNotAppliedMeans: answers that arrived AFTER their turn was released as abandoned: this loop reports them and applies nothing, so a row that says `abandoned` cannot gain records retroactively
turnLoop.turnInFlightMeans: inFlight is the LOOP's one-turn lock, not a promise about the durable ledgers: a second kernel over the same workspace answers inFlight:false while this one is busy, and `human.recover` reports inflight.pending from the DURABLE side (run 64 read pending:0 while a turn was stuck here - both readings were true). The in-flight turn names itself and its age; `vibe_vmu_turn { op:"abandon" }` closes it by name and releases the lock.

skippedTotals.means: this total is BOUNDED to the turn rows the ledger still retains, not to the session. `fields` sums the `skipped` entries of those rows (one entry = one field a kept turn did NOT execute, whatever the reason; it counts EVENTS, so the same field skipped in two turns counts twice - dedupe the `field`s out of `turnReceipts` yourself if you need names), `fieldsDispatchThrown` sums their `skippedFields` entries (the per-turn key of that name: ONLY the fields whose dispatch threw, so the two differ whenever something was skipped for its shape, for a missing meeting, as a duplicate, or with no face wired), and `turnsWithSkips` counts the rows that skipped at least one. `retainedTurns`/`evictedTurns` come from that same row array and the loop's own turn registry (turns ever opened minus rows retained), never from separate counting. Read `evictedSkippedUnknown` before trusting the numbers: when `evictedTurns` is 0 every turn this loop ever opened is still on the ledger and this total IS the session so far; when it is greater than 0 the retainer has already dropped that many old rows and how many fields THEY skipped is not recoverable from here - `fields` is then neither a session total nor an upper bound, only the retained part, and a total smaller than yesterday is that eviction, not a session that un-skipped anything. `counts.notExecuted` counts the same events for the whole process lifetime (it does NOT shrink when rows evict) but carries no per-turn attribution, so it can tell you the session-wide count and never which turns it belongs to.

status.skippedTotalsMeans: the SUM the per-turn ledger could not give without paging: `fields` counts skipped-field EVENTS across the retained turn rows (same field skipped twice counts twice), `fieldsDispatchThrown` the subset whose dispatch threw, `turnsWithSkips` the rows that skipped at least one field. `scope:"retained-turn-rows"` is the bound, and `evictedSkippedUnknown:true` means rows have already been dropped, so `fields` is only the retained part - not a session total and not an upper bound
status.turnLoopMeans: THIS IS THE LOOP'S OWN FACT, not a copy of the durable fold: `inFlight` true means one turn is holding the single-turn slot right now, `inFlightForMs` says for how long, and past `abandonAfterMs` this loop closes that turn BY NAME (or immediately with op:"abandon"). A reader who sees inFlight:true while the durable fold says nothing is pending is looking at exactly the run-64 contradiction - the fix is op:"abandon", not a retry
status.turnReceiptsMeans: HOST BOOKKEEPING, not the member's intent: this list records what the TURN LOOP observed while settling a turn (fields dispatched, fields skipped + code, writes with ids, refusal codes). It does not restate what the member meant, and a member that ran tools in its own child session can have done more than the row shows - `unavailable` names that gap. Rows are bounded to the last 50 turns; `turn` is the t-<n> id, `openedBy` says which door opened it (drive/activation/wait/null). RUN 250: each row ALSO carries the prompt/delivery evidence the run receipt shows - `notices` is {lines, rendered, blockChars} for the block that was in that turn's prompt (so "did the delivery render" is checkable per turn, not by scanning the workspace), `truncated`/`excerptLen` describe the receipt's own cut, `emptyReply`/`replyBytes` describe what the member wrote, and when a reply was cut past `vmu.turn.replyLimitChars` the full text lives at `replyFullPath` with `replyFullSha256`/`replyFullBytes` (verify them against the real file). null is a NAMED absence - "this loop has no reading for it (yet)"; `replyArchiveWhy` names why a cut reply has no full-text file (no archive seam wired, or the seam refused), and null there means there was nothing to warn about. RUN 251 (task-77): two more sentences a reader needs. (a) NAMES: the ONE authoritative names for the receipt cut are `truncated` and `excerptLen` — `replyTruncated` and `replyExcerpt` are the turn RECEIPT's older names for the same facts, kept here by name so old readers can find them and deliberately NOT duplicated as row keys; `excerptLen` is the CHARACTER COUNT of the cut (the excerpt TEXT itself is the receipt's `replyExcerpt`). (b) WHERE: row-level keys are `truncated`, `excerptLen`, `emptyReply`, `replyBytes`, `replyFullPath`, `replyFullSha256`, `replyFullBytes`, `replyArchiveWhy`; the block reading is the NESTED object `notices` = {lines, rendered, blockChars}, so `lines` is a key of `row.notices`, not of the row. `emptyReply`…[elided]
status.closureVoteLocalMeans: the closure votes written by THIS orchestrator, one row per member, each carrying the instant it was written and the session it came from. The kernel merges these over the durable fold rows so a receipt read straight after a vote is not one write behind itself; the durable rows remain the institute-wide truth and are the only ones another kernel reads
status.solvedThisRoundMeans: the raw per-round `solved` readings of this session, one per member that emitted the field - INCLUDING seats that hold no closure-vote permission (they appear here and never count toward closure; `closureVote` is the counted tally). It is the per-round convergence reading, NOT the closure vote: use `closureVote` for "is the question judged solved"

closureVote.windowMeans: the map is this orchestrator's, but every vote is also written to the durable fold key "closure_votes", so it spans the INSTITUTE. `missing` means "no recorded judgement" this reading can see; a member who voted in ANOTHER session IS visible here through that fold
closureVote.rulingReading: NOT here: cast/votesCast are the CLOSURE vote; the DEBATE ruling is `vibe_v5_verdict_final`
closureVote.castMeaning: cast === confirmed: every enfranchised member judged it solved; NOT "votes were cast" — see votesCast for arrivals
closureVote.notEligibleMeans: members who judged but hold no closure-vote permission: recorded, neither counted nor listed as missing
closureVote.votersMeans: who voted, one row per member, the LATEST judgement wins
closureVote.reason: silence blocks the CLOSURE VOTE (unanimity on「每个有投票权的成员都判定该问题已解决」) — it does NOT block closing the meeting (close rails: vmu.meetings.*; never decides close legality). Waiting: r-acad, r-1, r-2

status.liveReadingsMeans: the paper/blueprint/closure groups the LAST assembled status block carried, produced by the same statusReadingsFor call that built that block (so prompt and receipt cannot drift). Each group is {value|null, why, source, detail, at, atSource, timeWhy}: a null value names WHY the group is absent (no paper row, no bound meeting, an unreadable ledger), `source` names the ledger row/face that answered, and `at`/`timeWhy` say whether the content had a timestamp. `detail` is the derived reading (paper: status/round/missing/participants; blueprint: status/revision/mdPath/draftMdMissing/mdChangedSinceIndex; closure: votesCast/votesTotal/votesFor/votesAgainst/motionsPending). It is DERIVED from the durable rows on every assemble and never stored, so it cannot become a second truth source

turns.deliveryUnavailableMeans: 投递不可用（why:not-configured）：本轮成员未运行，任何写入都不是成员在自己的会话里完成的（所办代转或不可证），所以 workShareOf 把这一行的 write 计入 unknownActs，不算成员发言。

skippedTotals.means: this total is BOUNDED to the turn rows the ledger still retains, not to the session. `fields` sums the `skipped` entries of those rows (one entry = one field a kept turn did NOT execute, whatever the reason; it counts EVENTS, so the same field skipped in two turns counts twice - dedupe the `field`s out of `turnReceipts` yourself if you need names), `fieldsDispatchThrown` sums their `skippedFields` entries (the per-turn key of that name: ONLY the fields whose dispatch threw, so the two differ whenever something was skipped for its shape, for a missing meeting, as a duplicate, or with no face wired), and `turnsWithSkips` counts the rows that skipped at least one. `retainedTurns`/`evictedTurns` come from that same row array and the loop's own turn registry (turns ever opened minus rows retained), never from separate counting. Read `evictedSkippedUnknown` before trusting the numbers: when `evictedTurns` is 0 every turn this loop ever opened is still on the ledger and this total IS the session so far; when it is greater than 0 the retainer has already dropped that many old rows and how many fields THEY skipped is not recoverable from here - `fields` is then neither a session total nor an upper bound, only the retained part, and a total smaller than yesterday is that eviction, not a session that un-skipped anything. `counts.notExecuted` counts the same events for the whole process lifetime (it does NOT shrink when rows evict) but carries no per-turn attribution, so it can tell you the session-wide count and never which turns it belongs to.

receipt.turnsMeans: HOST BOOKKEEPING of each turn the loop settled (or still has open), NOT the member's intent: executed = reply fields dispatched and the face.op channel, skipped = fields kept but not executed (each with a code), writes = tool writes with their record ids, codes = refusal codes, unavailable = what this kernel CANNOT see (e.g. tool calls a member made in its own child session). `openedBy` says which door opened the turn: drive (the caller's step/drive), activation (the background pump), wait (a meeting wake), null (unknown/legacy). Bounded to the last rows; an empty list means no turn settled in THIS kernel session, not that nothing happened.
receipt.turnsUnavailableMeans: HOST BOOKKEEPING, not the member's intent: this list records what the TURN LOOP observed while settling a turn (fields dispatched, fields skipped + code, writes with ids, refusal codes). It does not restate what the member meant, and a member that ran tools in its own child session can have done more than the row shows - `unavailable` names that gap. Rows are bounded to the last 50 turns; `turn` is the t-<n> id, `openedBy` says which door opened it (drive/activation/wait/null). RUN 250: each row ALSO carries the prompt/delivery evidence the run receipt shows - `notices` is {lines, rendered, blockChars} for the block that was in that turn's prompt (so "did the delivery render" is checkable per turn, not by scanning the workspace), `truncated`/`excerptLen` describe the receipt's own cut, `emptyReply`/`replyBytes` describe what the member wrote, and when a reply was cut past `vmu.turn.replyLimitChars` the full text lives at `replyFullPath` with `replyFullSha256`/`replyFullBytes` (verify them against the real file). null is a NAMED absence - "this loop has no reading for it (yet)"; `replyArchiveWhy` names why a cut reply has no full-text file (no archive seam wired, or the seam refused), and null there means there was nothing to warn about. RUN 251 (task-77): two more sentences a reader needs. (a) NAMES: the ONE authoritative names for the receipt cut are `truncated` and `excerptLen` — `replyTruncated` and `replyExcerpt` are the turn RECEIPT's older names for the same facts, kept here by name so old readers can find them and deliberately NOT duplicated as row keys; `excerptLen` is the CHARACTER COUNT of the cut (the excerpt TEXT itself is the receipt's `replyExcerpt`). (b) WHERE: row-level keys are `truncated`, `excerptLen`, `emptyReply`, `replyBytes`, `replyFullPath`, `replyFullSha256`, `replyFullBytes`, `replyArchiveWhy`; the block reading is the NESTED object `notices` = {lines, rendered, blockChars}, so `lines` is a key of `row.notices`, not of the row. `emptyReply`…[elided]

started.alreadyMeans: `already` is the KERNEL's answer about ITS OWN start in THIS process — it registers the declared middleware and does nothing else, so `true` does NOT mean the institute existed before this call. Whether an institute existed is answered by `rosterBefore` (empty = nothing was there) and `hiredNow` (who this call minted).
started.means: this block is the PROJECTION of the kernel's start answer (same keys as `startedRaw`, minus nothing); the sentence that gives `already` its subject is `alreadyMeans`

receipt.startedMeans: `started` is the KERNEL's own answer about its middleware start: `already:true` means `kernel.start()` had ALREADY RUN IN THIS PROCESS (it registers the declared middleware and nothing else) — it is NOT a statement that the institute existed before. What THIS call seeded is `hiredNow` (the seats it created just now) and `rosterBefore` (who was on the roster when it began); an empty `rosterBefore` with `already:true` is a normal first founding in a process whose kernel was already started
receipt.leaderIdMeans: `applied` records the settings THIS call changed on ITS OWN kernel. `vmu.turn.leaderId` is one of them, and it is a PER-KERNEL setting: a member works in a different kernel/process, which does not inherit it, so a member's prompt can read leaderId as empty and fall back to the chair SEAT (the charter's leadership section names the chair) — that fallback is by design, not a broken setting. No face can push a setting into another kernel; `vibe_v5_configure` changes it for THIS process only, and its receipt says the same

receipt.hint: 两条合法路：①先写成命题卡 `vibe_v5_record_proposition { id, title, statement, value, motive, p, proof_ref:"Members/<m>/Propos/<id>.md#正式证明", proof_state:"complete" }`，再以卡 id 召集辩论；②把证明写成文件，以**文件引用**（路径或 .md/.lean/.txt/.tex/.json 名）作对象。本闸对卡核"有没有登记证明"、对文件核"可读且非空"，内容是否写完由辩论中的人核。 REACHABLE INSTEAD (the actor matters): this is an ADDRESS problem, not a proof problem — the sentence has no place to keep its proof, so the reachable repair is to give it one (register it as a card whose proof_ref/proof_state are set, or write the proof to a file and pass the file reference). No member turn can do that FOR you and the office must not type a member's proof: if the sentence came from a member, wake that author (vibe_vmu_turn { op: "drive", members: ["<author seat>"], rounds: 1 } with a next_step asking for the card and its proof_ref) — the rejected call here cannot be repaired by retrying it

procedure.title: 辩论会议 · 推荐流程骨架
procedure.subject: 辩论对象：命题卡 id（须含已写完的正式证明/证伪或已通过的 Lean 行）、一个文件引用（如 Members/<成员>/Propos/<id>.md 或 Lean 文件）。一句话命题不是对象。lean 已通过但概率仍非 1 的命题，辩论焦点是「代码中的命题与定义是否符合原意」。

steps.what: 各成员各自独立表态：给出该命题当前的布尔概率([0,1])、理由、以及证明/证伪进展。先不互相反驳、不互相引用（「独立」是**尽力而为的约定**，不是内核保证的隔离 —— 见 notes）。

展开辩论：轮流发言 / 举手后发言 / 主席邀请发言。★ 轮数由院士自行决定；本部署只给**动议次数**设了上限 `vmu.meetings.verdictMaxRounds`（默认 3，**任何 kind 的动议都计入**：topic/procedural/resolution 同占额度，程序动议会吃掉一轮辩论）——到限后新增动议会被具名拒 `VMU_RESOURCE_BUDGET`；额度只由这个设置决定——`extend` 延长的是发言、`extendlimit` 延长的是墙钟，两者都不增加动议额度，关会再开一场是另一场会议（额度从头算）。★ `extend`/`silent`/`end`/`hands` 是 primitive 原语，SERVICE 会议上具名拒 `VMU_REGISTRY_BOUNDARY`（primitive 注册表与 SERVICE 会面互不相通），发言界改读 `vibe_v5_say` 回执的 `speechBound`。

会议结束前，每位参加辩论的成员用 `vibe_v5_verdict` 交最终裁决：「布尔概率([0,1])，理由」——传 `meeting` + `proposition_id`（**不要传 `target`**：`target` 只认活票箱的 id，命题卡 id 会被具名拒）、`member` 填自己；主席可以用 `vibe_v5_verdict_ask` 通知还没交的人。★ 别把它和票箱混起来：`vibe_vmu_meeting { action: "ballot" }` 的票箱只对「待核验对象」开放——它的**决定性**票只认 1/0（(0,1) 的读数必须显式写 `estimate` 类型、且不进裁决均值）；票箱不是裁决通道，裁决汇总只读成员交上来的裁决卡（`vibe_v5_verdict_final` 的 `rulingSubmissions`）。
tools: vibe_v5_verdict { meeting: "<本会议>", proposition_id: "<命题卡 id>", verdict: <0..1>, member: "<你>" }
vibe_v5_verdict_ask { meeting: "<本会议>", proposition_id: "<命题卡 id>" }

steps.what: 框架裁定并通知：若全部一致为 1（或一致为 0）则最终概率取该值，否则取所有裁决的平均值；随后通知该命题卡的持有者把卡片概率改为该值。
tools: vibe_v5_verdict_final { meeting: "<本会议>", proposition_id: "<命题卡>", verdicts: [{ member, p, reason }], fidelity?: "conform" | "defect" }

notes: 本骨架是**推荐**：院士可以只做其中一步、改变顺序、或完全不用。框架不检查、不阻断、不记录偏离。

「单次发言版群聊」在本框架里就是「每人各说一次、互不打断」：会议内用 `vibe_vmu_meeting { action:"speak" }`（进会议记录），群聊形态用 `vibe_v5_say`。★ 但「独立」只是**尽力而为的约定**，两条事实要一起看：(a) 框架没有并发，轮次是**顺序**推进的（`kernel/turn` 的 drive 一个成员接一个成员跑），caller 交付模式下更是一格一回合（交回一份提示词、等一份回复，同一时刻只有一个待回回合），提示词装配也**不注入**别人的发言；(b) **即使顺序化、即使不注入前文，读房间仍然可能** —— `vibe_vmu_chat` 走 `chat.list`，内核的聊天读面**不按调用者过滤**，任何成员都能读到整个房间，包括同一轮里别人刚说的话。所以第 1 步的「独立」不是隔离保证：要隔离请用会议发言（进会议记录，工具面没有会议记录的读面）；靠群聊就只能靠这条约定。
发言楼层（谁先说话）是另一套机制：`vibe_vmu_meeting { action:"flow" }`（open/hands/round_robin/call_on）。骨架管议程，flow 管顺序，两者互不替代。
第 4 步不是自动的：`vibe_v5_verdict_final` 由**主席**显式调用（裁决必须有签名人），内核面 `vmu.meetingverdict` 只做算术与校验，通知走既有 mailbox 面 —— 本 pack **没有**在 `meetings.close` 上挂任何自动聚合钩子（"会议关了就把数算出来"会把一次显式裁定变成一次静默推断）。

receipt.procedureNote: 这套骨架是**推荐**，不是门禁：院士可以跳过、改序或完全不用，框架不检查也不阻断。

receipt.agendaItemsSourceMeans: `agendaItems` are the lines THIS face joined into the stored materials (an array agenda keeps its items; a one-line agenda is split on the "; " separator the join itself uses). The kernel meeting object keeps its own agenda items (ids ag-1..., closable one at a time) and the kernel face reads them back — this field never claims to be that ledger.
receipt.formalAgendaItemsWhy: no per-item agenda was recorded: this meeting never declared a formal agenda, so there is no item list to read (the agenda, if one was given, is the `materials` line — read `agendaItems`)
receipt.formalAgendaItemsHint: to record a per-item formal agenda, convene the meeting AGAIN and pass an ARRAY of items through the pack door: vibe_v5_meeting { formal_agenda: ["<item>", { title: "<item>", kind: "review" }] } — that is the front door (its schema accepts a boolean OR an array), so the items are validated and stored by the pack; from the kernel face the same array is open({ formalAgenda: [...] }). A boolean (formal_agenda:true, or formalAgenda:true) only DECLARES the agenda formal and leaves the items as the materials line
receipt.formalAgendaItemsMeans: null: this meeting carries NO per-item formal agenda. The convene face stores the agenda as ONE text line in `materials` (an array is joined with "; ") and `formal_agenda` there is a BOOLEAN "the agenda came from a formal block" flag, not an item list — so null is the absence of an item list, NOT an empty agenda: read `agendaItems` for the items
receipt.nonAttendingMeans: these members are ON the roster but a deployment declaration (vmu.meetings.attendDeniedSeats: temp) forbids their seat to attend or vote: an attempt to attend is refused BY NAME, and the unanimity reading does not wait for them

invitation.means: the appointment notice is DURABLE MAIL (channel "mail", kind "meeting-appointment") written ONCE, by the kernel open(), never by this face: every member in `delivered` will see it at their next turn or through vibe_v5_inbox, and the notice line it renders carries the exact attend call. `woken` is always [] here — a wake is a live nudge and the durable row is the promise; whether this deployment injects a wake seam is a deployment fact, not a silence (RUN 198). `unreachable` lists the members whose row did NOT go out, with the kernel own reason; the convene still succeeded and the meeting is readable, so the repair is a message to that member — never a second convene, and a delivery failure must never roll back an academic act

receipt.noticesMeans: notified / notifyRows / notifyFailed are the kernel open() receipt fields, passed through unchanged (the kernel wrote the durable rows, so there is exactly ONE row per invited member and ONE notice line): `notified` names the members that really got a row, `notifyRows` names the mail ids, `notifyFailed` names every member that did not with the kernel reason. This face sends no invitation of its own — a second sender would be a second row
receipt.typeMeans: `type` decides the PROCEDURE (which skeleton this meeting follows) and is the word the institute uses; `kind` is the meeting BOARD label (sync/division/verify-request/solve-vote) and is what an archive files the row under. When no kind was passed the label is DERIVED from the type where the type names one (debate→verify-request, closure→solve-vote, division→division) and `kindSource:"derived-from-type"` says nobody chose it; a type with no natural label falls back to "sync" with `kindSource:"default"`. Either way it is a filled-in label, not a reading of what the meeting was
receipt.kindSourceMeans: no kind was passed, so the framework DERIVED "verify-request" from type "debate" — the label an archive reader would expect. No caller chose it: pass kind explicitly to override
receipt.rosterMeans: the roster is the INVITATION LIST of this meeting (who was convened), not the bench. rosterNarrowed:true means convene was given an explicit subset (`members`, or a non-empty `roster`) and the meeting read back exactly those members; benchSize is how many live members the deployment had when it was convened (0 = this deployment exposes no membership seam, so no narrowing can be shown). The CHAIR is seated by opening even when it is not on the list — that is why `present` can name a member outside `roster`; `attend()` later adds a member, and then the roster is the invitation PLUS the members who joined. `eligible` is who may vote: the declared voter seats (vmu.meetings.eligibleSeats) intersected with THIS meeting roster, or the whole roster when no seat rule is declared. A count cannot answer "who": these fields are the ids themselves.
receipt.atSourceMeans: no `at` was passed: the meeting opened at the kernel clock, not at a declared time
receipt.requiresChairProceedMeans: false: the meeting is already running — proceed() has nothing left to open; act in it (speak/vote/hand)
receipt.startReadsMeans: startsInMs is non-null ONLY while the meeting has not started (positive = the start time is still in the future, negative = it is overdue); elapsedSinceMs is non-null ONLY once it has started (>= 0, measured from the moment it ACTUALLY opened, i.e. activatedAt — not from scheduledFor); elapsedMs is an alias of elapsedSinceMs kept for old readers (null while not started, never negative). TWO instants are in play and they are NOT the same fact: `openedAt` is the ATTENDANCE BASELINE (the due time, i.e. scheduledFor, fixed when the meeting was scheduled) and `activatedAt` is when the meeting REALLY became runnable (the touch that completed the attendance rule, or the chair proceed). A scheduled meeting that had to wait therefore has openedAt earlier than activatedAt, and `startedLate` says so; `lateReads.openedAt` on an attend receipt is the baseline, and null while the meeting has not started
receipt.lateAdmissionMeans: lateAdmission is THIS meeting policy for a late arrival (a late arrival is decided by vmu.meetings.lateAfterMs against openedAt): "open" seats a late member and records late:true; "chair" holds the member at the door (pendingLate) until the chair calls admit(); "refuse" refuses the late arrival by name and names the two repairs (the chair admits, or the member joins the next meeting). THE DEFAULT IS "chair": a late arrival is institutionally a request to be seated, so the chair decides it, and the hold is readable as pendingLate instead of the member slipping in unseen. "open" is the permissive policy and "refuse" the closed one; a meeting row that was opened before this default carries its own recorded value and is not retroactively changed.
receipt.wallLimitNote: the meeting’s OWN upper bound, frozen at open: `wallLimitMs` is the value, `wallLimitMsSource` says who froze it (`convene` = the chair set it with durationMs, `vmu.meetings.hardLimitMs` = the deployment default), and `extendlimit` can raise it later: extensions ADD to the current bound, and a request that would pass `vmu.meetings.extendCeilingMs` (this deployment declares no value, so the runtime ceiling applies; the refusal itself prints the ceiling it used, as `after / ceiling`) is refused BY NAME (`VMU_RESOURCE_BUDGET`) — nothing is clamped to the boundary. `extendCeilingMs` is the ceiling in effect for THAT refusal.
receipt.sequenceMeans: the meetings after this one were declared IN THIS CALL: `index` is this meeting's position (0-based), `total` counts it, and `next` is the SEQUENCE ROW of the meeting that follows (`{type,kind,subject}` - the declaration, not an id: an id exists only once that meeting is actually convened, and the driver takes the row, convenes it, and reads the new id from the open receipt; null = last). procedure.title: 辩论会议 · 推荐流程骨架
procedure.subject: 辩论对象：命题卡 id（须含已写完的正式证明/证伪或已通过的 Lean 行）、一个文件引用（如 Members/<成员>/Propos/<id>.md 或 Lean 文件）。一句话命题不是对象。lean 已通过但概率仍非 1 的命题，辩论焦点是「代码中的命题与定义是否符合原意」。

steps.what: 各成员各自独立表态：给出该命题当前的布尔概率([0,1])、理由、以及证明/证伪进展。先不互相反驳、不互相引用（「独立」是**尽力而为的约定**，不是内核保证的隔离 —— 见 notes）。

展开辩论：轮流发言 / 举手后发言 / 主席邀请发言。★ 轮数由院士自行决定；本部署只给**动议次数**设了上限 `vmu.meetings.verdictMaxRounds`（默认 3，**任何 kind 的动议都计入**：topic/procedural/resolution 同占额度，程序动议会吃掉一轮辩论）——到限后新增动议会被具名拒 `VMU_RESOURCE_BUDGET`；额度只由这个设置决定——`extend` 延长的是发言、`extendlimit` 延长的是墙钟，两者都不增加动议额度，关会再开一场是另一场会议（额度从头算）。★ `extend`/`silent`/`end`/`hands` 是 primitive 原语，SERVICE 会议上具名拒 `VMU_REGISTRY_BOUNDARY`（primitive 注册表与 SERVICE 会面互不相通），发言界改读 `vibe_v5_say` 回执的 `speechBound`。

会议结束前，每位参加辩论的成员用 `vibe_v5_verdict` 交最终裁决：「布尔概率([0,1])，理由」——传 `meeting` + `proposition_id`（**不要传 `target`**：`target` 只认活票箱的 id，命题卡 id 会被具名拒）、`member` 填自己；主席可以用 `vibe_v5_verdict_ask` 通知还没交的人。★ 别把它和票箱混起来：`vibe_vmu_meeting { action: "ballot" }` 的票箱只对「待核验对象」开放——它的**决定性**票只认 1/0（(0,1) 的读数必须显式写 `estimate` 类型、且不进裁决均值）；票箱不是裁决通道，裁决汇总只读成员交上来的裁决卡（`vibe_v5_verdict_final` 的 `rulingSubmissions`）。
tools: vibe_v5_verdict { meeting: "<本会议>", proposition_id: "<命题卡 id>", verdict: <0..1>, member: "<你>" }
vibe_v5_verdict_ask { meeting: "<本会议>", proposition_id: "<命题卡 id>" }

steps.what: 框架裁定并通知：若全部一致为 1（或一致为 0）则最终概率取该值，否则取所有裁决的平均值；随后通知该命题卡的持有者把卡片概率改为该值。
tools: vibe_v5_verdict_final { meeting: "<本会议>", proposition_id: "<命题卡>", verdicts: [{ member, p, reason }], fidelity?: "conform" | "defect" }

notes: 本骨架是**推荐**：院士可以只做其中一步、改变顺序、或完全不用。框架不检查、不阻断、不记录偏离。

「单次发言版群聊」在本框架里就是「每人各说一次、互不打断」：会议内用 `vibe_vmu_meeting { action:"speak" }`（进会议记录），群聊形态用 `vibe_v5_say`。★ 但「独立」只是**尽力而为的约定**，两条事实要一起看：(a) 框架没有并发，轮次是**顺序**推进的（`kernel/turn` 的 drive 一个成员接一个成员跑），caller 交付模式下更是一格一回合（交回一份提示词、等一份回复，同一时刻只有一个待回回合），提示词装配也**不注入**别人的发言；(b) **即使顺序化、即使不注入前文，读房间仍然可能** —— `vibe_vmu_chat` 走 `chat.list`，内核的聊天读面**不按调用者过滤**，任何成员都能读到整个房间，包括同一轮里别人刚说的话。所以第 1 步的「独立」不是隔离保证：要隔离请用会议发言（进会议记录，工具面没有会议记录的读面）；靠群聊就只能靠这条约定。
发言楼层（谁先说话）是另一套机制：`vibe_vmu_meeting { action:"flow" }`（open/hands/round_robin/call_on）。骨架管议程，flow 管顺序，两者互不替代。
第 4 步不是自动的：`vibe_v5_verdict_final` 由**主席**显式调用（裁决必须有签名人），内核面 `vmu.meetingverdict` 只做算术与校验，通知走既有 mailbox 面 —— 本 pack **没有**在 `meetings.close` 上挂任何自动聚合钩子（"会议关了就把数算出来"会把一次显式裁定变成一次静默推断）。

agendaItems: 仿真：票箱裁决（只压机制，不裁决数学）
receipt.agendaItemsSourceMeans: `agendaItems` are the lines THIS face joined into the stored materials (an array agenda keeps its items; a one-line agenda is split on the "; " separator the join itself uses). The kernel meeting object keeps its own agenda items (ids ag-1..., closable one at a time) and the kernel face reads them back — this field never claims to be that ledger.
receipt.formalAgendaItemsWhy: no per-item agenda was recorded: this meeting never declared a formal agenda, so there is no item list to read (the agenda, if one was given, is the `materials` line — read `agendaItems`)
receipt.formalAgendaItemsHint: to record a per-item formal agenda, convene the meeting AGAIN and pass an ARRAY of items through the pack door: vibe_v5_meeting { formal_agenda: ["<item>", { title: "<item>", kind: "review" }] } — that is the front door (its schema accepts a boolean OR an array), so the items are validated and stored by the pack; from the kernel face the same array is open({ formalAgenda: [...] }). A boolean (formal_agenda:true, or formalAgenda:true) only DECLARES the agenda formal and leaves the items as the materials line
receipt.formalAgendaItemsMeans: null: this meeting carries NO per-item formal agenda. The convene face stores the agenda as ONE text line in `materials` (an array is joined with "; ") and `formal_agenda` there is a BOOLEAN "the agenda came from a formal block" flag, not an item list — so null is the absence of an item list, NOT an empty agenda: read `agendaItems` for the items
receipt.nonAttendingMeans: these members are ON the roster but a deployment declaration (vmu.meetings.attendDeniedSeats: temp) forbids their seat to attend or vote: an attempt to attend is refused BY NAME, and the unanimity reading does not wait for them

invitation.means: the appointment notice is DURABLE MAIL (channel "mail", kind "meeting-appointment") written ONCE, by the kernel open(), never by this face: every member in `delivered` will see it at their next turn or through vibe_v5_inbox, and the notice line it renders carries the exact attend call. `woken` is always [] here — a wake is a live nudge and the durable row is the promise; whether this deployment injects a wake seam is a deployment fact, not a silence (RUN 198). `unreachable` lists the members whose row did NOT go out, with the kernel own reason; the convene still succeeded and the meeting is readable, so the repair is a message to that member — never a second convene, and a delivery failure must never roll back an academic act

receipt.noticesMeans: notified / notifyRows / notifyFailed are the kernel open() receipt fields, passed through unchanged (the kernel wrote the durable rows, so there is exactly ONE row per invited member and ONE notice line): `notified` names the members that really got a row, `notifyRows` names the mail ids, `notifyFailed` names every member that did not with the kernel reason. This face sends no invitation of its own — a second sender would be a second row
receipt.typeMeans: `type` decides the PROCEDURE (which skeleton this meeting follows) and is the word the institute uses; `kind` is the meeting BOARD label (sync/division/verify-request/solve-vote) and is what an archive files the row under. When no kind was passed the label is DERIVED from the type where the type names one (debate→verify-request, closure→solve-vote, division→division) and `kindSource:"derived-from-type"` says nobody chose it; a type with no natural label falls back to "sync" with `kindSource:"default"`. Either way it is a filled-in label, not a reading of what the meeting was
receipt.kindSourceMeans: no kind was passed, so the framework DERIVED "verify-request" from type "debate" — the label an archive reader would expect. No caller chose it: pass kind explicitly to override
receipt.rosterMeans: the roster is the INVITATION LIST of this meeting (who was convened), not the bench. rosterNarrowed:true means convene was given an explicit subset (`members`, or a non-empty `roster`) and the meeting read back exactly those members; benchSize is how many live members the deployment had when it was convened (0 = this deployment exposes no membership seam, so no narrowing can be shown). The CHAIR is seated by opening even when it is not on the list — that is why `present` can name a member outside `roster`; `attend()` later adds a member, and then the roster is the invitation PLUS the members who joined. `eligible` is who may vote: the declared voter seats (vmu.meetings.eligibleSeats) intersected with THIS meeting roster, or the whole roster when no seat rule is declared. A count cannot answer "who": these fields are the ids themselves.
receipt.atSourceMeans: no `at` was passed: the meeting opened at the kernel clock, not at a declared time
receipt.requiresChairProceedMeans: false: the meeting is already running — proceed() has nothing left to open; act in it (speak/vote/hand)
receipt.startReadsMeans: startsInMs is non-null ONLY while the meeting has not started (positive = the start time is still in the future, negative = it is overdue); elapsedSinceMs is non-null ONLY once it has started (>= 0, measured from the moment it ACTUALLY opened, i.e. activatedAt — not from scheduledFor); elapsedMs is an alias of elapsedSinceMs kept for old readers (null while not started, never negative). TWO instants are in play and they are NOT the same fact: `openedAt` is the ATTENDANCE BASELINE (the due time, i.e. scheduledFor, fixed when the meeting was scheduled) and `activatedAt` is when the meeting REALLY became runnable (the touch that completed the attendance rule, or the chair proceed). A scheduled meeting that had to wait therefore has openedAt earlier than activatedAt, and `startedLate` says so; `lateReads.openedAt` on an attend receipt is the baseline, and null while the meeting has not started
receipt.lateAdmissionMeans: lateAdmission is THIS meeting policy for a late arrival (a late arrival is decided by vmu.meetings.lateAfterMs against openedAt): "open" seats a late member and records late:true; "chair" holds the member at the door (pendingLate) until the chair calls admit(); "refuse" refuses the late arrival by name and names the two repairs (the chair admits, or the member joins the next meeting). THE DEFAULT IS "chair": a late arrival is institutionally a request to be seated, so the chair decides it, and the hold is readable as pendingLate instead of the member slipping in unseen. "open" is the permissive policy and "refuse" the closed one; a meeting row that was opened before this default carries its own recorded value and is not retroactively changed.
receipt.wallLimitNote: the meeting’s OWN upper bound, frozen at open: `wallLimitMs` is the value, `wallLimitMsSource` says who froze it (`convene` = the chair set it with durationMs, `vmu.meetings.hardLimitMs` = the deployment default), and `extendlimit` can raise it later: extensions ADD to the current bound, and a request that would pass `vmu.meetings.extendCeilingMs` (this deployment declares no value, so the runtime ceiling applies; the refusal itself prints the ceiling it used, as `after / ceiling`) is refused BY NAME (`VMU_RESOURCE_BUDGET`) — nothing is clamped to the boundary. `extendCeilingMs` is the ceiling in effect for THAT refusal.
receipt.sequenceMeans: the meetings after this one were declared IN THIS CALL: `index` is this meeting's position (0-based), `total` counts it, and `next` is the SEQUENCE ROW of the meeting that follows (`{type,kind,subject}` - the declaration, not an id: an id exists only once that meeting is actually convened, and the driver takes the row, convenes it, and reads the new id from the open receipt; null = last). Advancing is decided by the call that declared them, not by a settings key, so `enforced` names no policy for it.

receipt.note: the original could also PROPOSE a meeting from a non-chair seat and let the chair convene it; this face has no propose path (named gap: procedure/propose). ★★ THIS FACE ONLY CONVENES: for status/summary/snapshot/close/extend/extendlimit/proceed/lapse/ballot/speak/hand/hands/order/invite/invitedspeak/attend/flow/overrideorder use vibe_vmu_meeting { action, id } - the kernel face, which reaches the same meeting object. Measured on a full live run: an agent tried summary/close HERE, got nothing, and reported it as a missing capability; the capability existed one face over and nothing said so. ★ D9 邀请面 (this round): hand/invite/invitedspeak/order/attend now really reach a SERVICE meeting through that face — hand = a member queues itself, invite = the CHAIR puts one member or an ordered list (members:[…]) on the floor queue, order = reads the real queue back, invitedspeak = the invited voice speaks in the minutes, attend = marks a member present (an invitation NEVER marks anybody present: attendance is its own act and only it counts for the quorum). silent/end/hands stay primitive-only and the kernel face refuses them on a service meeting BY NAME. ★ A floor-order override (flow/overrideorder) still needs vmu.meetings.orderMode declared by the deployment; v5r does not declare it, so on a real run it is refused by name rather than silently ignored. ★ The recommended procedure is a RECOMMENDATION: skipping it, reordering it, or ignoring it entirely is allowed and unchecked.
receipt.callerIsSeatMeans: this key answers ONE question: did this call run from the named seat and its own session? It does not say whether the seat carried the act out - that is what a delivered turn (turnReceipts, deliveryPath) answers
receipt.ranInOwnTurnMeans: true when this call ran from the seat own session, or when the kernel reported that a turn for this seat was actually DELIVERED and returned (out.turnDelivered) - the two facts that one key used to conflate
receipt.memberActedMeans: this call ran from the OFFICE (a root session, which is not a seat) and named member "r-acad": the record was written IN THAT SEAT'S NAME, but the seat did not act in its own turn. `memberActed:false` states that difference - orchestrating on a seat's behalf is not the same act as carrying it out, and a reader who needs the seat's own judgement should ask for it in a turn of that seat

receiptMeta.note: NOTHING was elided by us: this receipt is over MAX_TOOL_RESULT_BYTES (12000) but no string leaf exceeded 2000, and meeting the budget would require dropping content, which would change its shape. `originalBytes` is the real size. quorum.capUniverseMeans: the denominator is this meeting's eligible members (4), because the ATTENDANCE floor can never exceed who was invited — the rule's vote floor is reported separately in voteFloor
quorum.capPolicy: min(quorumMin/quorumRatio need, vmu.meetings.quorumCap, eligible members of this roster) — the ATTENDANCE floor; the rule's 表决 floor is voteFloor.effective
quorum.presentNote: present = chair (seated by open(), so the house can transact at all) + members who attended or voted; presentBreakdown splits them, and `unanswered` names who has done neither
quorum.metIs: the FLOOR question only (present >= required) — it is NOT the institution rule; with required=0 it is true while nobody has attended. Read unanimity.met / the pack rule for the real threshold
quorum.metPolicy: met = (present >= required) — the FLOOR question (may this house transact at all); it deliberately does NOT fold in the institution's unanimity rule, because `met` gates vote() and requiring full attendance before the first vote would deadlock the house. unanimity.deniedSeatsDeclaredMeans: the seats the deployment DECLARED as non-attending (vmu.meetings.attendDeniedSeats): a declaration, not a count — `nonAttending`/`nonAttendingSeats` name the members of THIS roster that the declaration actually removes
unanimity.nonAttendingMeans: no member of this roster sits in a seat that the attendance declarations forbid
unanimity.policy: the institution's rule is unanimity: the quorum counts as established only when EVERY roster member has attended or voted AND the floor is met (「未到齐则法定人数不成立」); the electorate is the roster minus the seats that vmu.meetings.attendDeniedSeats forbids to attend: such a seat cannot be barred from the meeting and waited for at the same time, so the ELECTORATE of that "every" excludes it — those members are NAMED in `nonAttending`, never silently dropped
unanimity.because: the floor is not met: present 2 < required 3

voteFloor.effectiveNote: the lower bound for a ruling is min(max(quorumMin, ceil(quorumRatio*roster)), quorumCap, eligible universe) — see formula; this is 表决人数 (rule L47), and it is NOT the attendance floor (`required`)
